answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from costly, non-transferable identity: every agent must post a real bond locked for a long vesting window. To forge a thousand fakes, an attacker funds a thousand parallel bonds, tying up capital that earns nothing while identities age. Nodes check these stakes against long-lived reputation history, not peer vouches, so a fresh jade cluster cannot replace a verified record. Double-signing triggers slashing, and like a jetty narrowing a river's mouth, admission filters sybil waves into a thin stream. Cost scales linearly, reward does not.
